$meta.name: Industry
$meta.description: An industrial-HUD SKIN: cool concrete under a technical grid, square panels cut at 45deg, charcoal chips, and one hazard yellow. Generated into dist/jrk-skin-industry.css by scripts/build-tokens.mjs. Never hand-edit dist/.
$meta.$axisNote: THIS IS NOT A THIRD THEME. It has its own light and dark halves, so it is orthogonal to the light/dark axis and is stamped separately: `data-skin="industry"` crossed with `data-theme="light"|"dark"` (or the OS setting). Four blocks, not one. Anyone who reaches for `data-theme="industry"` will get nothing — the generator emits no such selector, and it cannot, because that stamp has nowhere to put the second half of this palette.
$meta.$scopeNote: COLOUR AND SHADOW ONLY. The chamfers, the squared controls, the wedge and the wide label tracking live in css/skins/industry.css, which holds no colour at all. That split is not tidiness: tokens.json is the only source of truth for design values, so every hex is here; geometry is component behaviour, so it is in CSS. Neither file can do the other's job.
$meta.$measuredNote: Every ratio in a $note below was computed by hand against the panel — #f4f6f6 light, #1e2224 dark — and the inks that land on the page were checked at BOTH ends of the gradient. scripts/validate-skin.mjs re-derives them on every `npm test`; it does not trust these strings.
$meta.$chartNote: The skin does NOT override one chart slot and that is a measured decision, not an omission. Its light panel (#f4f6f6) is darker than the base card (#ffffff), so every light mark loses about 8% contrast — slot 1 goes 4.02 to 3.70, slot 5 4.13 to 3.81, slot 6 3.65 to 3.36. No slot crosses the 3:1 mark floor and reliefRequired.light is unchanged, so the CVD-derived palette carries over intact. Dark IMPROVES slightly (#1e2224 is darker than #232326). What DID have to move is chart.chrome.surface: it is stroked as the ring around a dot, so leaving it at the base card would have painted a white ring on a #f4f6f6 panel — the same defect this library already recorded when that token sat at a stale #1c1c1e.

variantAxis.$note: THE ATTRIBUTE, DECLARED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. It was hardcoded in build-tokens.mjs until 2026-08-25, when vitrine gained a colour choice of its own and `hazard` stopped being the right word for every skin: this skin's hue is a hazard SIGNAL, vitrine's is a MATERIAL, and they stamp data-hazard and data-tint respectively. Nothing about this skin changed — the emitted selectors are byte-identical — but the name is now a fact in the token file instead of an assumption in the generator. `default` is yellow, and yellow is the ABSENCE of the attribute rather than a value of it.

$varsNote: Keyed by the CSS variable name WITHOUT the --jrk- prefix, deliberately. The generator's own naming is namespace-specific (color.text.onBanner -> text-on-banner, font.family.sans -> font-sans, chart.chrome.surface -> chart-surface), so a mirror of tokens.json's tree would need a second, divergent mapping table. Instead the build ASSERTS that every name here already exists in the base layer; a typo or a renamed base token fails `npm run build` instead of emitting a colour nothing reads. Skin-only names go in `skinOnly`, which is exempt from that assertion and is the only way to add one.

surface-canvas.$note:
A GRADIENT, which is legal only because every consumer sets it with the `background` shorthand (base.css, auth.css, shell.css) — a `background-color` would drop it silently. It also means NOTHING can be validated against 'the page': every ink that lands here is held to the DARK end. The ramp is monotonic and both inks are outside the span, so the endpoints bound the interior.

THE LIGHT HALF WAS LIGHTENED ON 2026-08-20 TO BUY THE DOT GROUND ITS CONTRAST, and it moved WITH surface-default — the two are a pair here and neither may move alone. The old ramp was #eceeee -> #e2e5e6 -> #d6dadb under a #f4f6f6 panel. The dot texture is held to text-muted on this ramp's dark end, and on #d6dadb that ceiling was alpha 0.050, which paints a dot at 1.10:1 — measurably there and visually not. On #e4e7e7 the ceiling is 0.115 and the dot lands at 1.26:1. Lightening the page ALONE would have paid for that out of the tile's enclosure: clip-path deletes this skin's card shadows, so the panel-over-page fill step and the hairline are the whole boundary, and the step was 1.30:1. Lifting the panel to #ffffff in the same move holds it at 1.24:1. Going further is possible and it is the enclosure that pays: #e8ebeb buys alpha 0.130 and leaves 1.20:1.

THE LIGHT TOP WAS TAKEN TO PURE WHITE ON 2026-08-24, BY DIRECTION: white at the head of the ramp settling into the concrete grey near the bottom. THE DARK END DID NOT MOVE (#e4e7e7), which is what makes the change cheap — every figure in this file is held to the dark end, so the dot ground's alpha 0.115 ceiling, text-muted at 5.68:1 and the 1.24:1 panel step are all unchanged. The grey now ARRIVES at 88% and holds, rather than being reached only at the last pixel.

WHAT IT COSTS IS THE PANEL STEP AT THE TOP OF THE PAGE, AND THE HAIRLINE PAYS IT BACK: surface-default is #ffffff, so a tile at the head of the ramp has a 1.00:1 fill step — the state the base library records as a shipped failure — and clip-path deletes this skin's card shadows, so there is no third channel. IT IS SAFE HERE ONLY BECAUSE border-subtle IS REAL AND GETS STRONGER AS THE STEP DIES: #d3d8d9 is 1.16:1 on the ramp's grey end and 1.44:1 on white. The two channels trade places down the page rather than both fading, which is the opposite of the failure case (a 1.00:1 step behind a TRANSPARENT border). Never let border-subtle go transparent under this skin, and if the panel ever has to bound itself by fill again, the top stop is what moves — #fcfcfc restores a 1.02:1 step and still reads as white.

EVERY OTHER LAYER IMPROVED. The dot ground is masked to the LOWER band and lands on unchanged pixels. The wave, which was masked to the UPPER band, gained the most from the lightening (1.13:1 with text-muted at 6.25:1, against 1.12:1 / 5.07:1) and was then REMOVED ON 2026-08-25 by direction - near the top of the port its arcs read as horizontal dashes, and a white top is what made that obvious. The top band of this ramp now carries no texture at all. The stripe's yellow band 1 goes 1.03:1 to 1.28:1 against the page where it crosses the top, which is the one place that chroma-only band is visible in greyscale at all.

surface-default.$note:
The panel, and the surface every ratio in this file is measured against. Lifted from #f4f6f6 to #ffffff on 2026-08-20 as the other half of the page-lightening — see surface-canvas for why they moved together. 1.24:1 off the page's dark end in light (was 1.30:1), 1.20:1 in dark, so the panel does NOT bound itself and border-subtle is load-bearing in both halves.

It now EQUALS surface-raised in light, which is deliberate and is the base library's own arrangement — surface.raised.light is #ffffff there too. Nothing gates that pair; what is gated is raised-hover, disabled, card-hover and subtle against this one, and all four still step. Every dark ink on the panel improved by the lift, and every LIGHT thing on it got harder: the chart marks are the ones to watch, and validate:skin re-checks the 3:1 mark floor on this value on every build. Moving toward white moves back toward the surface the base palette was derived on, so the slots gained margin rather than losing it.

surface-subtle.$note: 1.14:1 recess off the panel in light, 1.16:1 in dark. text.muted is 5.58:1 on it in light and 6.12:1 in dark, so a table header's own label clears on both.

surface-raised.$note: Popovers only. Pure white is the ONE place this palette uses it — the panel is #f4f6f6, so a menu reads as lifted off the card rather than equal to it, which is the failure the base library recorded when raisedHover equalled raised.

surface-banner.$note: FLAT CHARCOAL, not a ramp. The base masthead's three-stop gradient carries a middle stop that fails and is kept empty by layout; this skin declines that bargain outright, so the topbar's contrast is a colour fact again rather than a layout fact. text-on-banner is 11.38:1 on it.

surface-raised-hover.$note: Deliberately NOT equal to surface-raised in either half — that equality is on this library's record as the bug that left menus with no hover at all.

surface-card-hover.$note: A REAL step in both halves — 1.14:1 light, 1.30:1 dark — and it has to be, because css/skins/industry.css neutralises shadow-card and shadow-card-raise on every notched tile: clip-path clips the box-shadow, so a chamfered card cannot carry one. The base library's arrangement (shadow in light, fill in dark, each a no-op in the other) is not available here. The fill is the whole hover in both halves.

surface-disabled.$note: Checked against the panel it sits on, which is the other equality this library has shipped twice: #e2e5e6 vs #f4f6f6 and #151819 vs #1e2224, so a disabled control is a real step in both halves.

text-primary.$note: 16.59:1 on the panel light, 13.23:1 dark. On the page: 15.45 / 12.77 light, 15.85 dark.

text-muted.$note: 6.51:1 / 5.50:1 on the panel — but the binding surface is the PAGE, and that is what set these values. #5d686d measured 5.28:1 on the panel and 4.07:1 at the page's dark end, i.e. it passed everywhere a single-hex check would have looked and failed on the bottom third of the screen; the dark candidate #7c8689 failed the same way at 4.30:1. Re-step against the page, never the panel.

text-disabled.$note: 2.88:1 / 2.80:1, under the floor and exempt from it (WCAG 1.4.3 excludes inactive controls). It is the one ink here that is allowed to fail.

text-inverse.$note: Ink for surface-inverse, so it runs OPPOSITE to text-primary. Not interchangeable with accent-on-solid, which is #14171a in both halves.

text-link.$note: A DEEP OLIVE-GOLD in light, and it looks nothing like the accent on purpose — see accent-text. 6.00:1 on the panel and 4.62:1 at the page's dark end. Dark takes the brand stop itself at 12.57:1.

border-subtle.$note: 1.33:1 / 1.20:1 against the panel. Load-bearing in BOTH halves here, because the panel-to-page step is only 1.30:1 / 1.20:1 — this skin has no half where a fill step alone bounds a tile.

border-strong.$note: 5.28:1 / 5.13:1 — well over the 3:1 a meaningful boundary owes. #6f797c and #7c8689 were the first picks at 4.12 and 4.30, kept for reference.

border-accent.$note: THE ACCENT EDGE IS A DARK GOLD IN LIGHT, NOT THE BRAND YELLOW, and this is the single most surprising value in the file. #ffe500 as an edge on the panel is 1.18:1 — invisible — and the hue does not reach 3:1 until #a08d00 (3.07:1). Since border-accent is what says SELECTED on a segment or a tab, a yellow edge would have made the chosen control indistinguishable from the unchosen one in the light half. Dark has no such problem and keeps the brand stop.

accent-solid.$note: The same value in both halves, which nothing else in this file does. Its behaviour is what changes: 1.18:1 against the light panel and 12.57:1 against the dark one.

accent-solid-hover.$note: Separated from the resting fill by CHROMA only — there is no luminance room left on this hue. A hover that has to be felt rather than seen belongs on the shadow or the fill beneath, not here.

accent-on-solid.$note: BLACK in both halves, at 14.10:1. White on this fill is 1.28:1. There is no light ink for this colour, so unlike the base library's accent this token has no direction to flip and re-measuring it after a hue change means re-checking whether the hue is still usable at all.

accent-text.$note: The reason the four accent roles are NOT one value here, which is the opposite of the base library's arrangement. The brand stop clears 4.5:1 in none of them in light: as text on the panel the deepest step of the hue that does is #6b5e00 at 6.00:1, and as an edge it is #a08d00 at 3.07:1. So light needs a separate step per role and dark takes the anchor for all of them.

accent-wash.$note: Black is 16.09:1 on the light wash and text.muted still clears at 5.12:1 — the one hazard surface muted ink survives.

accent-wash-border.$note: 1.46:1 on the light panel, and kept far below border-accent so a wash-filled control never looks selected.

status-good-text.$note: 6.65:1 on the panel and 6.02:1 on its own wash. The mark itself is only 4.48:1 on that wash, which is why the .text role exists.

status-warning-mark.$note: A BURNT ORANGE, and it has to be: the accent is already yellow, so a yellow warning cannot read as a warning here. 4.84:1 / 7.75:1.

status-warning-text.$note: 6.48:1 on the panel, 5.71:1 on its own wash — the mark is 4.26:1 there and fails.

status-serious-mark.$note: 6.97:1 / 6.90:1. Sits between warning and critical in hue as well as in name.

status-critical-text.$note: 6.24:1 on the panel, 5.54:1 on its own wash.

status-critical-solid.$note: White is 5.58:1 on it. Kept as its own token rather than borrowed from the accent, because accent-on-solid here is black and a danger button must not take its ink direction from a yellow.

focus-offset.$note: The bloom's backing, i.e. the colour the focus ring is measured to sit on. Tracks surface-default for the same reason chart-surface does, and moved with it on 2026-08-20.

chart-surface.$note: The surface every chart mark is measured against. Tracks surface-default and validate:skin fails if it drifts — it is stroked as the ring around a dot, so a stale value paints the wrong colour rather than nothing. Moved to #ffffff with the panel on 2026-08-20.

shadow-card.$note: Near-absent by design: this skin states depth with the hairline, the chamfer and the grid. In dark it is `none` because a black shadow on #111314 renders nothing, so the fill step and the border carry the whole enclosure there.

shadow-card-raise.$note: The GAP between this and shadow-card is what makes a card respond to the pointer. Point them at the same value and an interactive tile goes dead in light, where surface-card-hover is only a 1.07:1 lift.

shadow-focus.$note: TWO-TONE, and the order swaps by theme so the OUTER band always contrasts with the plane behind it. A yellow-only ring is the same 1.18:1 as the fill — it would have been the one focus indicator in the system and it would have been invisible in light. Nothing validates a colour inside a shadow string, so both bands were measured by hand: #14171a is 16.59:1 on the light panel, #ffe500 is 12.57:1 on the dark one.

font-sans.$note: A CONDENSED grotesque is what carries the technical read. Authored as a themed pair with one value so it goes through the same emitter as everything else; css/fonts.css loads the family. Inter remains the fallback, so a CSP that blocks the font host degrades to the base face rather than to a system serif.

tracking-caps.$note: The signature: an 11px uppercase label at 0.14em. Legible only BECAUSE it is uppercase and short — the base value is tighter, and this one must never reach sentence-case copy or a value the reader has to compare.

radius-data-end.$note: The end cap on a bar, meter or progress fill. Squared here — a rounded cap reads as a gauge and this palette's marks are machined.

vars.$radiusNote: SQUARE IS THE DEFAULT AND THE NOTCH REPLACES THE RADIUS — the inversion of the base library's control ladder. radius-full is deliberately NOT overridden, because it is the only thing keeping a dot a dot, a spinner a circle and a radio round; .jrk-btn--icon reads as this skin's charcoal CHIP for the same reason. css/skins/industry.css squares the named controls that would otherwise stay pills, and that named list is the skin's contract: anything new that opts into radius-full stays a pill under the skin until it is added there.

skinOnly.$comment: Names with no base counterpart, exempt from the build's exists-in-base assertion. Every one of them is referenced from css/skins/industry.css — a value here that nothing reads is dead weight, and nothing else will tell you.

surface-canvas-grid.$note:
The technical grid. DOTS AT THE INTERSECTIONS rather than continuous lines (2026-08-20) - the reference look's ground is a dot field. Drawn as a masked radial-gradient tile by the skin stylesheet; hand-recorded because nothing measures a colour inside a gradient.

THE ALPHA IS PINNED BY text.muted ON THE PAGE'S DARK END, not by moire, and this note used to say otherwise. The old 'roughly 0.09, it moires against an 11px label' ceiling is real but it is the SECOND constraint. On the pre-2026-08-20 ramp (dark end #d6dadb) the contrast ceiling was 0.050 - BELOW the moire figure - and the dot it painted was 1.10:1, which is measurably present and visually absent. That is what the page lightening was for: on #e4e7e7 the ceiling is 0.115. At 0.10 the dot lands at 1.22:1 with text.muted at 4.64:1 and text.secondary at 6.54:1. Dark has more room and takes 0.13 - 1.35:1, muted 4.88:1.

*** THE BUDGET IS NO LONGER SHARED. *** Until 2026-08-25 a second fixed layer - the wave, concentric arcs masked to the UPPER band - split these pixels with the dots. It was removed by direction, because near the top of the port those arcs are wide and nearly flat and read as horizontal dashes rather than as a bloom. The two were masked COMPLEMENTARILY, dots below the horizon and wave above, so a dot never composited on top of an arc and each layer got the full ceiling; overlap them and the alphas ADD, which on the light half put muted under the floor. With one layer left there is nothing to overlap and the whole 0.115 is available, so there is headroom from the shipped 0.10 if the dots ever need to read harder. REACH FOR THE RADIUS FIRST ANYWAY: radius is free against a per-pixel contrast floor and alpha is not. AND THE ADDING RULE HAS NOT GONE AWAY - it was never about the wave specifically. Any new translucent layer on these pixels spends this budget again and has to be measured against what is already there, not against the page.

surface-glow.$note:
THE ILLUMINATION AT THE WIPE'S LEADING EDGE — the bloom that travels with the reveal on .jrk-hovercard--materialize, so the panel reads as loading in rather than being uncovered. Transient decoration, drawn as a gradient on a pseudo-element, so hand-recorded: nothing measures a colour inside a gradient.

DARK IS THE EFFECT AND LIGHT IS A SUBSTITUTE, because YOU CANNOT ILLUMINATE WHITE. The hovercard's panel is surface-raised, which in light is #ffffff — pure white, and deliberately so; its own note explains that it is the one place this palette uses pure white, to lift a popover off the #f4f6f6 card. A white glow there measures 1.00:1. Not faint: absent. There is no brighter-than-white to bloom toward, so no re-stepping fixes it and the request cannot be met literally in that half.

SO LIGHT TAKES THE BRAND YELLOW AT 1.28:1, WHICH IS A CHROMA-ONLY SIGNAL, and it is only defensible because the effect is REDUNDANTLY ENCODED. The same edge also carries the hard scanline bar in border-accent, which is 3.33:1 on this panel and therefore visible in greyscale, to a monochromat and in print. The bloom is the colour half of a two-channel signal, not the signal. If the bar is ever dropped, the light half of this glow becomes decoration nobody can see and should be dropped with it.

Dark takes the real thing: #ffffff at 13.52:1 on the #2b2f31 panel. No contrast floor applies to either — this is never a ground for ink and it is gone in about 320ms — so the figures above are visibility, not safety.

surface-canvas-stripe.$note:
THE STRIPE — ONE near-vertical band cut across the whole viewport, with a three-step darkening face along its trailing edge so it reads as an extruded bar. Four bands in one gradient. Decoration. Hand-recorded, because nothing measures a colour inside a gradient.

IT TRACKS THE HAZARD HUE, so all four bands are declared in every variant. The default (the ABSENCE of data-hazard) is yellow.

BOTH HALVES DERIVE FROM accent-wash, AND THAT IS THE FIRST TIME THIS TOKEN HAS HAD ONE RULE RATHER THAN TWO. Light band 1 is the light wash, dark band 1 the dark wash, and each face step is the band before it scaled by 0.88 per sRGB channel. The vivid accent-solid was DIRECTED into the light half on 2026-08-20, so the stripe would match the hue swatch in the gallery picker, and SOFTENED BACK OUT on 2026-08-25, also by direction: the light stripe was to read as quietly as the dark one already does. Dark did not move and never could — dark page ink is near-white and a vivid fill cannot carry it (#e6eaea on #ffe500 is 1.05:1).

*** THE LAYOUT CONDITION IS GONE, AND IT IS WHAT THE SOFTENING BOUGHT. *** With the vivid fill, red, purple and blue in LIGHT could not be crossed by page text at all — near-black measured 3.88:1 / 2.95:1 / 3.92:1 on the fill and 1.93:1 / 1.62:1 / 1.96:1 on the deepest face, so what shipped was a promise about layout of the .jrk-topbar--brand kind, and nothing gated it. Every wash carries near-black at 11.6:1 or better BY DERIVATION, so the wash-derived ramp clears text-primary on every band of every hue in both halves: worst 5.46:1 (purple band 4), and per hue, band 1 to band 4 — yellow 16.09 / 12.29 / 9.43 / 7.31, orange 11.64 / 8.94 / 6.95 / 5.48, red 11.80 / 9.07 / 7.06 / 5.52, purple 11.67 / 8.97 / 6.98 / 5.46, blue 11.64 / 8.98 / 6.93 / 5.47, green 12.09 / 9.31 / 7.22 / 5.63. This library has ONE layout-dependent contrast fact again, the base topbar brand ramp, and this is no longer it.

THE RAMP LENGTH IS CHOSEN RATHER THAN LEFT OVER, which is the second thing the wash bought. Pinning band 1 to the vivid fill made the extrude as long as the gap between that fill and the ink floor, so GREEN’S EXTRUDE BARELY READ — its fill is only 6.19:1 on near-black to begin with, the legal range was #09ae5c to #08944e, and the three steps were nearly one colour. A wash starts far from the floor, so the 0.88 walk is a free choice: separations run 1.27:1 to 1.31:1 in light against the dark half’s 1.13:1 to 1.51:1, in every hue, and the extrusion reads without the ramp having to reach for anything.

SECONDARY AND MUTED still do not survive the deep steps in either half — secondary is 3.02:1 to 4.04:1 on band 4. ONLY text-primary is safe anywhere on the assembly; what changed is that it is now safe on ALL of it, for all six hues, in both halves.

VISIBILITY IS THE PRICE AND IT IS ALSO THE POINT. Light band 1 is 1.12:1 / 1.06:1 / 1.11:1 off the page ramp’s three stops for yellow and 1.20:1 to 1.55:1 for the other five, against 1.03:1 and 2.02:1 to 4.90:1 before — so every hue now separates from the page largely by CHROMA, and the light assembly is invisible in greyscale and in print. Same finding as accent-solid at 1.18:1 on the panel and masthead-fill at 1.02:1 to 1.11:1 on the page: under this skin a QUIET light mark is a chroma mark, because there is no luminance room between a pale hue and a near-white page. Suppressed in @media print either way. If a hue ever has to read in greyscale again, band 1 goes back to the vivid fill and the layout condition comes back with it — those are one decision, not two.

IT TOOK SIX SHAPES. Two corner wedges, whose edge angles came from their own box aspects and so were not parallel; a half-plane, which read as a slab rather than a mark; a band with one opaque face; a wash-derived four-band ramp; a vivid-derived one; and the wash again, gently stepped. The angle is stated ONCE in stripe-angle.

surface-canvas-stripe-shade-1.$note: THE FIRST STEP OF THE SHADED FACE. Three opaque steps, each darker than the last, replace what would otherwise be a drop shadow. A TRANSLUCENT SHADOW IS UNAVAILABLE AND BOTH HALVES SAY SO SEPARATELY: in dark, black over this page at alpha 0.20 measures 1.020:1 against the page's dark end, so it is invisible at any usable alpha - the base library's shadow.card-in-dark finding, this skin's own clip-path finding and midgard's inset bevel arriving at one conclusion by three routes, that on a dark ground elevation is a FILL. In light a shadow is legal in isolation (alpha 0.10 leaves text-muted at 4.64:1) but not on these pixels, because surface-canvas-grid already spends 0.10 of a 0.115 ceiling there and the alphas ADD. THAT REMAINS TRUE WITH ONE TEXTURE LAYER RATHER THAN TWO: the wave was removed on 2026-08-25 and its complementary mask went with it, which frees a budget the wave was NOT spending anyway - the two never shared a pixel by construction. The dot ground still spends 0.10 of 0.115 wherever it is drawn, so a translucent shadow over the lower band is still illegal. Opaque steps spend none of that budget. Derivation, per-hue values and the safe-ink rule are on surface-canvas-stripe.

surface-canvas-stripe-shade-2.$note: A DEEPER STEP OF THE SHADED FACE. See surface-canvas-stripe-shade-1 for why the face is opaque steps rather than a shadow, and surface-canvas-stripe for the derivation and the safe-ink rule. This step carries text-primary in both halves for all six hues and does NOT carry secondary or muted.

surface-canvas-stripe-shade-3.$note: A DEEPER STEP OF THE SHADED FACE. See surface-canvas-stripe-shade-1 for why the face is opaque steps rather than a shadow, and surface-canvas-stripe for the derivation and the safe-ink rule. This step carries text-primary in both halves for all six hues and does NOT carry secondary or muted.

skinOnly.$notchNote: The 45deg corner cut, applied with clip-path. ONE corner per panel, top-right by default. This is the token the base library has no equivalent of, and it is what makes the skin recognisable with the yellow removed — which matters, because the yellow is the one colour here that disappears in greyscale.

masthead-fill.$note: THE MASTHEAD FOLLOWS THE THEME as of 2026-08-24: a pale band in light, the dark banner in dark. It is stated as var() indirection rather than as literal hexes so that it cannot drift from the values it is derived from — and, under industry, so that data-hazard re-hues the masthead for free. NOT surface-banner in light: that token is the SHEET's metric block-head (css/components/sheet.css reads it in six places) and a light banner there would repaint every workbook header. The masthead needed its own namespace. The wash is the right light value because every one of the six hazard washes carries accent-wash-text (#14171a) at 11.64:1 or better BY DERIVATION — measured across all six: yellow 16.09, green 12.09, red 11.80, purple 11.67, orange and blue 11.64 — so the ink is safe for every hue with no per-variant work. *** IN LIGHT THIS BAND SEPARATES FROM THE PAGE BY CHROMA, NOT LUMINANCE: the yellow wash is 1.05/1.02/1.11 against the page ramp's three stops, so it is all but invisible in greyscale and in print. That is the third instance of this skin's own yellow finding, and it is why the hairline is load-bearing in light as well as dark. The five hazard hues carry more of a step (1.20-1.45) but none of them is a boundary either.

masthead-ink.$note: What --jrk-gradient-ink points at on the masthead, which re-inks every caption, status, ghost button and search field on the bar in one declaration. It is ALSO the focus ring: 11.64-16.09:1 on the light washes and 15.14/15.85:1 on the dark band, where accent-solid would have been invisible on a yellow band (#ffe500 on #fff59a). The base library reaches the same answer for the same reason — gradient.topbar.ring is black in light and white in dark.

masthead-brand-fill.$note: THE BRAND MASTHEAD IS WHITE IN LIGHT, where --vivid keeps the pale wash (masthead-fill). Directed 2026-08-24, and the split is what earns both: --vivid is a quiet tinted band, --brand is a white plate carrying bold hazard marks. Dark is the same charcoal banner for both. White is stated as surface-default rather than as a literal so it tracks the skin's own panel. WHAT IT BUYS is the mark budget: near-black ink is 17.99:1 on white against 16.09:1 on the yellow wash, and — far more importantly — the marks may run FULL vivid accent-solid instead of the stepped border-accent, because ink crossing a mark is measured against the MARK, not the band. Ceilings across the six hazard hues: yellow, orange and green take 100%, blue 90%, red 85%, purple 75%. So 75% is the number to respect, against 42% before. *** THE MARKS NO LONGER SPEND THAT BUDGET IN LIGHT. *** masthead-mark-strength halves them there as of 2026-08-25, by direction, so the ceilings above are headroom rather than a description of what ships — see that token. What white still buys is the OPTION: on the yellow wash the marks could not have run at full accent-solid at all, and on white they can, so the strength is a knob rather than a limit.

masthead-mark-strength.$note:
THE STRENGTH OF THE GLITCH FURNITURE, applied as `opacity` on the ::after that carries it — ONE value scaling the whole mask, which is the only way to move one half without restating thirteen fill-opacities per theme: the mask is a single data URI and both themes read it.

DARK IS 1 AND IS THE REFERENCE. On the charcoal band the marks composite to #736909 through #cfba03, 3.43:1 to 9.77:1, and read as dim technical noise.

LIGHT WAS HALVED ON 2026-08-25, BY DIRECTION — the marks were to read as softly as the dark ones do. THE MEASUREMENT TO CARRY IS WHY THEY DID NOT ALREADY: the light band is white (masthead-brand-fill), so the marks were 1.13:1 to 1.23:1 in luminance — quieter than the dark half by a factor of eight — and still the loudest thing on the bar, because what a saturated yellow does against pure white is a CHROMA jump and no contrast ratio sees it. Softening this half therefore means spending ALPHA, not lightness: at 0.5 the strongest yellow mark composites to #fff599 (1.12:1) and the character goes from highlighter to whisper. Across the six hazard hues the light marks now land at 1.06:1 to 1.99:1 on the white plate, against 1.13:1 to 4.33:1 before.

GOING DOWN IS FREE AND GOING UP IS NOT. Every figure on masthead-brand-fill is an upper bound (yellow, orange and green 100%, blue 90%, red 85%, purple 75%), so a lower strength only relaxes them; anything above 1 in either half needs the whole mark budget re-derived.

variants.$comment: HAZARD HUE VARIANTS. Stamped as a THIRD attribute — data-skin="industry" data-hazard="blue" — crossed with the theme, so the axes are skin x hazard x theme. Only the ACCENT namespace moves: the steel neutrals, the status set, the geometry and the type are the skin and do not vary. That is the point of the split — a hazard hue is a hue, not a design.
variants.$axisNote: The default is YELLOW and it is not a variant: an unstamped data-hazard leaves the skin exactly as it was, so no existing consumer changes and the yellow keeps the hand-derived values it shipped with. Every variant here is the FIVE other hues.
variants.$methodNote: Derived by search, not picked. Each hue is one HSL anchor plus a 1%-granularity lightness ramp, and every role is the NEAREST LEGAL STEP to that hue vivid centre — light roles darken, dark roles lighten, and each stops the moment it clears its floor. Cross-check on the method: run against yellow it reproduces the hand-derived shipped values to within one step (text #6b6000 vs #6b5e00, border #9e8e00 vs #a08d00), and the hand derivation was not consulted while writing it. scripts/validate-skin.mjs re-derives every ratio below on each build.
variants.$washNote: The washes are MIXES TOWARD THE PANEL from a floor of 0.5, not steps on the lightness ramp, and that is the one place the yellow misleads. What separates a wash from a fill on a pale hue is CHROMA: #ffe500 is already lighter than most panels, so a lightness walk returns the vivid stop itself and calls it a wash. No contrast ratio can catch that, because luminance is blind to chroma. Hence the fixed mix floor.
variants.$findingsNote: Three things the six hues taught, all of which read as rules about the DESIGN until you measure a second hue: (1) THE WEDGE-IS-INVISIBLE RULE IS A YELLOW RULE. Yellow is 1.17:1 on the light panel and green 1.38:1, so neither bounds itself — but red is 4.27:1, blue 4.23:1 and purple 5.62:1, and those three fills bound themselves and can be their own border.accent with no stepped value at all. (2) BLACK-INK-ALWAYS IS ALSO A YELLOW RULE. Yellow, orange and green take black; red, purple and blue take white, and no step of them takes black. (3) FIVE OF SIX SHARE ONE FILL ACROSS BOTH THEMES. Only purple has to lift in dark (#8f24db -> #9a3adf) to clear 3:1 on the dark panel. An earlier version of the search started the dark walk at the vivid stop rather than at the light fill and reported red and blue lifting too, WITH their ink flipping to black — black text on a mid-red, legal at 4.53:1 and plainly wrong. If a variant ever reports an ink flip, suspect the search before believing it.
variants.$cvdNote: INTER-VARIANT CVD SEPARATION IS NOT A REQUIREMENT HERE, and that is a real difference from the chart palette rather than a lowered bar. yellow/green collide at dE 8.8 and purple/blue at dE 4.3 — and it does not matter, because exactly one hazard is stamped at a time and two variants are never on screen together. A chart slot is POSITIONAL and its neighbours are present; a hazard hue is EXCLUSIVE. What does matter is each hue against the skin STATUS colours, which are on screen with it, and that is gated: an unacknowledged collision fails validate:skin.

red.$usageRule: THE ONE VARIANT WITH A RESTRICTION, and it is not fixable by re-stepping. A hazard red and this skin status reds are the same hue by construction — both are the deepest step of red where white ink survives — so under protanopia the accent and the danger signal collapse (dE 3.2 to 6.3). The rule that follows: with data-hazard=red, a critical or warning badge must carry its icon AND its label, never colour alone, and a .jrk-btn--cta must not sit in the same tile as a .jrk-btn--danger-solid. That is the base library rule about a lone blue series beside a --cta, one step more severe. If a view cannot honour it, pick another hue: orange is the nearest one that clears every status colour (dE 17.0 worst).
